name: Michael Paradinas
editorial_article: Michael Robert Paradinas (born 26 September 1971), widely recognized by his primary alias μ-Ziq, is a seminal English electronic musician, producer, and label owner from Wimbledon, London. A pivotal figure in the 1990s electronic music landscape, Paradinas gained early prominence for his contributions to the 'intelligent dance music' (IDM) scene. He made his debut in 1993 with the critically acclaimed album 'Tango n' Vectif', released on Aphex Twin's Rephlex Records. Paradinas is renowned for his prolific output under numerous aliases—including Tusken Raiders, Kid Spatula, Jake Slazenger, and Heterotic—which allowed him to explore diverse sonic territories ranging from complex drill 'n' bass to jazz-funk and experimental techno. His 1997 album 'Lunatic Harness' is frequently cited as a landmark work that helped define the drill 'n' bass subgenre. In 1995, Paradinas founded the influential record label Planet Mu. Initially established as a sublabel under Virgin Records, it eventually evolved into an independent powerhouse that has championed boundary-pushing electronic genres, including juke and footwork. Throughout his career, Paradinas has collaborated with luminaries like Aphex Twin (notably as Mike & Rich) and his wife, Lara Rix-Martin, with whom he performs as Heterotic. His work continues to influence contemporary electronic music through its signature blend of intricate programming, melodic experimentation, and rhythmic innovation. Paradinas was born in London and began his musical journey in the 1980s, influenced early on by New Wave acts like OMD and Heaven 17, before transitioning to the electronic innovations that would define his career. His dedication to pushing boundaries and fostering new talent through Planet Mu has secured his legacy as one of the most important figures in modern electronic music.
